scenes.label: THIS WEEK
scenes.title: Redesigning the Tools Registry
scenes.subtitle: Week 2 · 16–20 November 2026
rows: Continued translating the client's POC screens into Frappe, using Frappe UI
Redesigned to match the Portal Core look and feel
Grid and list views, type filter, search and pagination, with sample data
New Tool and the calculation preview
scenes.text: Last week, I continued translating the client's proof of concept into our Frappe app, using Frappe UI, and redesigned the Tools Registry to match the Portal Core look and feel. Some parts now work with sample data, like the filter, search and pagination. Others, like New Tool and the calculation preview, are still static.
This is the redesigned Tools Registry. Each tool is a card, showing its type, version and category, and the card highlights when you hover over it.
The same tools can also be shown as a list.
The filter narrows the tools by type. The three types are now Frappe, Excel and third party, in line with the three sockets.
Search finds a tool by its name, standard or category, for example, the ARR rainfall tool.
Instead of endless scrolling, the registry now uses pages, with nine tools on each page, and the screen stays in place when you change pages.
Opening a tool shows its details, and a preview of how a calculation would run, marked Preliminary, subject to engineer review. This part is still static.

scenes.label: NEXT
scenes.title: What comes next
scenes.subtitle: Ahead of delivery on 11 December 2026
rows: Build the "New Tool" form to register a tool in Engineering Labs
Define each tool's type (Frappe, Excel, 3rd Party) and where it's reached
Add the tool's input and output fields (dynamic, per tool)
scenes.text: Next, I'll build the New Tool form, so a tool can be registered in Engineering Labs. It will capture the tool's details and type, whether Frappe, Excel or third party, and where the tool can be reached. It will also let us define the tool's input and output fields, which are dynamic for each tool. Thank you.
